tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read numbered UTF-8 lines. offset is one-based; limit defaults to 200. Use smaller ranges when output is truncated.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Create or replace a whole UTF-8 file and its parent directories. Use edit_file for partial changes to an existing file.

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Apply exact replacements to an existing file and return a unified diff. Each oldText must match exactly once in the original file, or set replaceAll to replace every occurrence; a unique match that differs only in leading or trailing whitespace on each line is accepted. Edits must not overlap; errors name each failing edit.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run bash. Every command starts in your working folder, so don't cd there first; a cd lasts only for that command. Unhandled failures stop the script (errexit and pipefail); use if or || for expected failures. Piping to head can cause SIGPIPE; use a draining filter such as sed -n instead. command is the shell script itself, not a bash -c/bash -lc invocation — put the script text directly in command. Use rg for search, run tests, and inspect git diff. timeout is seconds (default 120, maximum 600). A command still running at its timeout moves to the background and keeps running, and you get an event when it ends (one that starts with sleep is stopped instead). Set run_in_background up front for servers, watchers and anything you know is long: it returns at once with a task id and a log file, and the command is stopped after 30 minutes unless timeout says otherwise (up to 7200). Never wait with sleep: background tasks and messages wake you by themselves. Output up to 30,000 characters comes back whole; past that you get its start, its end and the path of the whole output. Every result ends with the exit status and how long the command took; tool updates contain output as it arrives. Files written by commands inherit the environment's resource limits.
